selected_evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created on node1 with shared writable, sticky (no cross-user delete) semantics via Ansible
selected_evidence.summary: Playbook written on node2 and executed against node1; resulting directory is drwxrwxrwt root:root (mode 1777)

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that users cannot remove files owned by other users
selected_evidence.summary: Two test users each created a file in /srv/drop; dropuser_bob's attempt to rm dropuser_alice's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' due to the sticky bit

selected_evidence.requirement: Implementation uses Ansible from a legitimate control node (node2) rather than local commands on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed node2 has ansible-core and used it with an inventory/playbook targeting node1 over SSH

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 901ef286...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id f8551547... (changed); /srv/drop permissions (1777 root:root) confirmed intact post-reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6fd57414...; reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id 0d4caa87... (changed); Ansible files and SSH connectivity to node1 confirmed functional via a successful idempotent playbook re-run (changed=0)

selected_evidence.requirement: Cluster remained functional end-to-end after both restarts
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart idempotent Ansible run from node2 against node1 reported ok=2, changed=0; final stat on node1 confirms /srv/drop is drwxrwxrwt root:root 1777
